source.exactGuideSentence: She has an understated but powerful screen presence.

source.sourceFidelity: The proposal retains the exact guide example as guide_original_example and labels its practice scenes as new situations; no source-question answer is asserted from the guide example.

sevenStepEditorialReview.reason: A alone describes restrained acting that holds attention; Chinese tracks the model and answer.
A–D are four defensible responses to a silent close-up; B alone uses screen presence.
B invents a loud speech and C credits lighting although the scene explicitly says a small reaction held the audience. They are contradictions, not plausible near misses.
C supplies no remembered performer, so the scene does not support screen presence; A/B do.
B asserts every long reaction shot is too slow and C says louder music makes acting irrelevant. Neither is a credible alternative reply to the director’s actual concern.
The exact cloze span is screen presence; the model and Chinese are aligned.

The prompt repeats the listening/scene/speaking pattern of a nearly silent close-up, tiny facial change and viewers continuing to watch. Naming recovery news and eight seconds is added detail, not a materially new setting, task or goal; it also resembles selected 2332’s small-smile film example.

traditionalChinese: All question prompts, options, model sentences, writing answers and takeaways have intelligible Traditional Chinese with no decisive key or polarity mismatch. Any revised content needs a fresh bilingual check; rendered line wrapping has not been assessed.

existingOwnerComparison.relationship: Selected light up the screen lesson already explains a performer drawing attention, including quiet scenes and a small smile. The new noun collocation can be separate, but the proposed claimed contrast is overstated and its examples strongly duplicate that owner.

requiredFixes: Re-author final writing as a different communicative task, such as a casting or review decision across a performance rather than another silent close-up; regenerate two complete examples and exact answer-derived glossary.
Replace scene/dialogue distractors with plausible partial explanations of the same footage.

Reword the owner boundary: screen presence describes a quality; light up the screen describes an effect, and restrained performances can satisfy both. Do not claim a mutually exclusive quiet-versus-vivid distinction.
verdict: REVISE — failed changed-context writing and weak scene/dialogue; resolve overlap with selected 2332 before selection.
limits: This is an editorial/source review of the exact local proposal. No audio clips were generated or heard; no browser, physical-device, backend, publication or rights-clearance gate was run.
